subject: Different plots sharing the same x-axis

messages.author: 2401d0740178cf07
messages.subject: Different plots sharing the same x-axis
parts:
Dear list subscribers,

I am trying to plot some meteorological data that shares the same x-axis (in this case, date). 

What I would like to do is to plot independent geom-line plots, but sharing the same x-axis. The result I want to achieve looks like this figure: http://origin-ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0022169411007256-gr2.jpg

Notice the different variables, with distinct y-axis range and labels.

Hadley said this was difficult to achieve using ggplot2 (https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/Align-two-plots-on-a-page), but it's been a while since then and things might have evolved.

Can anyone point any direction? The data I want to plot is data.frame "data" in the code:

library(reshape2)
library(ggplot2)    
require(RCurl)

# Read data
link<-getURL("https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/27700634/data.csv")
weather <- read.csv(textConnection(link),header=F, sep=',', stringsAsFactors = FALSE, as.is=TRUE)
names(weather) <- c('Year', 'Julian',  'Hour', 'Temperature', 'Net Radiation', 'Precipitation', 'Humidity', 'Wind')

# Combine the first three columns into a character vector
date_info <- with(weather, paste(Year, Julian, Hour))

# Parse that character vector
weather$date <- strptime(date_info, "%Y %j %H")

# Data is hourly, but I need daily averages (or accumulation, for precip)
# First, create factor for days
DF2 <- data.frame(weather, Day = as.Date(format(weather$date))) 

#Then, create daily averages and accumulation
new <- aggregate(cbind(Humidity, Temperature, Wind) ~ Day, DF2, mean)
tmp <- aggregate(cbind(Precipitation) ~ Day, DF2, sum)
new$Precipitation <- tmp$Precipitation

# Remove wind, not desired right now
new <- subset(new, select = -c(Wind))

# Melt data by date
data <- melt(new, id='Day')

Thanks in advance for any help,
Thiago.

> Hi Ista,

> Thanks a lot for the suggestions you made. The first one (geom_lines only)
> is exactly what was looking for, but there's a little problem that prevents
> me of using it.
>
> I haven't found any way to include independent y-axis labels for the plot.

I think the idea is that the facet labels serve this function.
Facetting in the other direction makes this a little clearer:

ggplot(data, aes(x = Day, y = value)) +
geom_line() +
facet_grid(variable ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
ylab("")

and of course you can recode the "variable" column with any labels you like.

If you really must have labels on the left I can't think of an elegant
solution. You can do something like

grid.text(label = c("y axis label 1", "y axis label 2", "y axis label 3"),
x = rep(.02, 3),
y = c(.225, .5, .8),
rot = 90)

but its not ideal.

Best,
Ista

> Yes, but then he showed you how to do it. And in your case you're
> already 90% there, all you need to do is plot it:
>
> ggplot(data, aes(x = Day, y = value)) +
> geom_line() +
> facet_wrap(~ variable, ncol=1, scales = "free_y")
>
> Or
>
> ggplot(data, aes(x = Day, y = value)) +
> facet_wrap(~ variable, ncol=1, scales = "free_y") +
> geom_line(data = subset(data, variable == "Humidity")) +
> geom_point(data = subset(data, variable != "Humidity"))
>
> Best,
